correctness.rationale: At \(\eta=1/a\), each scalar client reaches \(b_i\) after one step and all later local gradients vanish. The source normalization therefore gives \(d_i=(x-b_i)/(\eta\tau_i)\). Substitution into the source default server update yields an exact scalar affine map with multiplier \(-(\tau_1-\tau_2)^2/(4\tau_1\tau_2)\). Solving \(|M|<1\) gives the stated quadratic inequality and the roots \(3\pm2\sqrt2\). The \(1:6\) witness is exact rational arithmetic, not an experiment.

value.rationale: FedNova was designed specifically to neutralize heterogeneous local-work weighting. The accepted result isolates a complementary finite-step effect in the simplest possible setting: even when local optimization is perfect after one step, the default normalization-plus-rescaling can both invert the effective client weighting and cross a sharp stability frontier solely because the local step counts differ. The exact 1:6 onset and the closed fixed-point formula make the boundary directly interpretable for server-scale design and clarify why later work favors alternative local-step scaling.
